payload.default: Each job's output stream is capped at a reasonable limit (e.g., last 10,000 lines or 10MB in memory). If a job exceeds this, older output is discarded (ring buffer), and a warning is injected into the stream: 'j2 | [WARNING: output truncated, showing last 10K lines]'. Full output is always written to the job's worktree log file, with the summary table showing a link to the full log.
payload.text: One job in the parallel set produces massive output (100MB of logs from a failing test suite). The multiplexed output mechanism is buffering this in memory before display. What prevents OOM, and how does the user know output was truncated?
